note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, price and lighting answer below comes from the City of Cape Coral's own pages: its Park Sports/Games page for the counts, the lighting and the price, and each park's own page for the address and the amenities. Cape Coral publishes more about its pickleball in one document than almost any operator in this directory, and where it stays silent - on surface, on parking, on whether Sands Park is lit - this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking: Cape Coral publishes nothing about parking at any of these five parks. No lot, no capacity, no fee, no permit - the word does not appear on any of the five park pages, and this site does not fill it in from an aerial photograph. What the City does publish is enough to shape the trip anyway. Four of the five parks have restrooms, stated in their amenity lists: Camelot, Giuffrida, Jim Jeffers and Joe Stonis. Sands Park's page does not list them, and rather than read that as a no, this site records nothing. Three of the parks are substantial sites that plainly expect people to arrive by car and stay a while - Jim Jeffers is 18.7 acres in north-west Cape Coral with four lighted soccer fields, lighted basketball courts, three picnic pavilions and a three-acre lake; Joe Stonis is seven landscaped acres around a one-acre lake; Camelot is 6.4 acres with a paved perimeter walking path. Giuffrida, at 3.7 acres, is the smallest and the oldest, the first neighbourhood park the City ever built. The practical planning fact here is not parking but light: three of the five stay open to 9 p.m., and the other two close at sunset, which in south-west Florida is a much sharper deadline than it sounds.
slots.peak_hours: Cape Coral splits neatly in two on timing, and the City draws the line itself. Camelot Park, Jim Jeffers Park and Joe Stonis Park have lights and are "open until 9:00 p.m. daily". Giuffrida Park has no lights, stated outright, and Sands Park is not marked either way. Everything else runs on the City's general rule: its park courts are open "from sunrise to sunset (or later for locations with lighting)". So a weekday evening game in Cape Coral is possible at three of these five venues and impossible at one of them, and that is a published fact rather than an inference. In a city where summer afternoons are brutal, the lit courts are not a luxury but the main usable window. There is a second, subtler timing question at three of the five, and it has nothing to do with the clock. Camelot, Jim Jeffers and Joe Stonis are convertible: the City writes each of them as "Two (2) tennis courts -OR- Four (4) pickleball courts", one pair of slabs in two configurations. Whether you find four pickleball courts or two tennis courts depends on how they are set up and who arrived first. Only Giuffrida and Sands have dedicated pickleball courts that are pickleball courts whenever you turn up. What the City does not publish anywhere is when any of this is busy - no league night, no morning rush, no rotation rule of the kind Kirkland or Scottsdale posts. That silence is left as it is.
slots.surface_condition: The City names a surface exactly once in Cape Coral and it belongs to a tennis court: Burton Memorial Park's "One (1) asphalt tennis court - no lights", a venue with no pickleball and therefore no page here. For the five published venues nothing is said about what the courts are made of. What the City does distinguish, clearly and usefully, is something better: whether a court is a pickleball court or a tennis court doing duty as one. Giuffrida Park and Sands Park have "dedicated pickleball courts" in the City's own words - six courts between them where the net is at pickleball height and the only lines are the ones you want. The other three are tennis slabs that convert, and their pages say so rather than presenting four courts as though they stood on their own. The single most useful thing the City writes about the state of these courts is a negative. Giuffrida Park reads "Two (2) dedicated pickleball courts  - no lights", and an operator willing to write that down when it is true is an operator whose silences can be trusted. That is why Sands Park's missing lighting answer is recorded here as unknown and not quietly assumed.
slots.local_scene: Twenty verified courts across five parks, every one of them free. That last part is rarer than it should be: this directory records a price only when an operator publishes one, and Cape Coral is one of only two cities on the whole site with a verified free court, because the City states it plainly - its park pickleball courts are "available for public use at no charge". Sixteen of the twenty are lit or in lit parks, three venues stay open to 9 p.m., and six of the twenty are dedicated pickleball courts rather than converted tennis. The number this page cannot give you is the interesting one. The City lists a venue called The Courts with "32 dedicated pickleball courts and 12 tennis courts" - by a distance the largest count this project has read anywhere, more than the whole of published Cape Coral put together - and publishes no address for it and gives it no park page. It also sits underneath the City's own "no charge" sentence while being a paid facility on its operator's account. Two things this site requires are missing, so it is named here rather than listed, and the contradiction is written down rather than resolved. Two more venues fall short by one fact each. Gator Trails Park has two lighted dedicated courts and an address, "3628 Garden Blvd", that neither of this site's address resolvers can find. Four Freedoms Park has an address, an air-conditioned indoor court and a published price of $5 per person for two hours, and never says how many courts. So the real pickleball inventory of Cape Coral is far larger than twenty, and the gap is a gap in what the City writes down rather than in what it has built. Cape Coral is the first Florida city in this directory and the first in Lee County.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts under lights
best_for.text: Jim Jeffers Park is the largest published pickleball venue in Cape Coral with six courts - four on the lighted convertible tennis slabs and two warm-up courts the City counts separately. Open until 9 p.m., free, on an 18.7-acre site in north-west Cape Coral with restrooms, a three-acre lake, lighted soccer and basketball, and walking paths.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a real pickleball court
best_for.text: Sands Park has four dedicated pickleball courts - not tennis courts lent to the game - in a park with walking paths, a putting green, a burrowing owl habitat and a butterfly garden. Free. The one thing the City does not say about it is whether the courts are lit, so plan for sunset until that changes.

best_for.heading: Best if you play in daylight and want to know what you are getting
best_for.text: Giuffrida Park has two dedicated pickleball courts and the City states outright that there are no lights, so it closes at sunset. It is the only Cape Coral venue counted twice by the City, on the sports page and on the park's own page, and at 3.7 acres it is the oldest neighbourhood park in the city. Free, with restrooms.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Cape Coral have?
faqs.a: Far more than we can verify. We have confirmed 20 across five City parks: six at Jim Jeffers, four each at Camelot, Joe Stonis and Sands, and two at Giuffrida. The City also names a facility called The Courts with 32 dedicated pickleball courts, publishes no address for it, and lists two further pickleball sites we cannot publish.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Cape Coral?
faqs.a: Yes at all five venues here, and the City says so rather than leaving it to be assumed: its park tennis and pickleball courts are "available for public use at no charge". Cape Coral is one of only two cities on this site with a verified free court. Four Freedoms Park, which is not published here, charges $5 per person.

faqs.q: Which Cape Coral courts have lights?
faqs.a: Camelot Park, Jim Jeffers Park and Joe Stonis Park, all of which stay open until 9:00 p.m. daily. Giuffrida Park is stated to have no lights and closes at sunset. Sands Park is the one venue the City marks neither way, so its lighting is recorded here as unverified.

faqs.q: What does "Two (2) tennis courts -OR- Four (4) pickleball courts" mean?
faqs.a: It means one pair of tennis slabs that can be set up as four pickleball courts, not four pickleball courts standing alongside two tennis courts. Camelot, Jim Jeffers and Joe Stonis are all written this way. Giuffrida and Sands are different - the City calls their courts dedicated, so they are pickleball courts whenever you arrive.

faqs.q: Why is The Courts not listed, when it has 32 courts?
faqs.a: Because the City publishes no address for it and gives it no park page, and this site requires a street address that resolves. It is also listed underneath the City's sentence saying these courts are free while being a paid facility on its operator's own account. Two problems, both of them the record's rather than the venue's.

faqs.q: Why is Gator Trails Park not listed?
faqs.a: It has two lighted dedicated pickleball courts, which is more than the City states for some venues that do publish here. Its address, "3628 Garden Blvd", is not found by either of this site's address resolvers, and a venue at an address nobody can locate does not publish. It is the most expensive refusal in this city.

faqs.q: Are there indoor courts in Cape Coral?
faqs.a: The City names one: a portable indoor court at Four Freedoms Park, 4818 Tarpon Court, at $5 per person for two hours with a maximum of four players, and paddles available to borrow. It is not published here because the City never says how many courts there are.

Sunrise to sunset at Giuffrida and Sands, and sunrise to 9:00 p.m. at Camelot, Jim Jeffers and Joe Stonis. The City states the rule once for all of its park courts: open "from sunrise to sunset (or later for locations with lighting)".

Under "Court locations include:": Camelot Park, Jim Jeffers Park and Joe Stonis Park each "Two (2) tennis courts -OR- Four (4) pickleball courts with lights - open until 9:00 p.m. daily", Jim Jeffers adding "and two (2) warm-up pickleball courts"; Gator Trails Park "Two (2) dedicated pickleball courts with lights"; Giuffrida Park "Two (2) dedicated pickleball courts  - no lights"; Sands Park "Four (4) dedicated pickleball courts"; The Courts "32 dedicated pickleball courts and 12 tennis courts"; Burton Memorial Park "One (1) asphalt tennis court - no lights". Four Freedoms Park (4818 Tarpon Court) offers "the portable indoor court" at "$5 per person (maximum of 4 players at a time) to reserve 2 hours of playtime". sources.evidence: The five published addresses were matched at house-number level and placed in the incorporated place "Cape Coral", Lee County, FL. Four resolved through OpenStreetMap rather than the Census address file: three because the Census changed the street type - Cape Coral has parallel Streets, Terraces and Lanes at the same house number - and one because the Census holds no record of Ceitus Parkway. "3628 Garden Blvd", the address the City publishes for Gator Trails Park, is found by neither resolver. Snapshot: data/sources/capecoral-county-census.json
